newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police seize $75 million in Mafia assets.
newsitem.headline: Italian police seize $75 million in Mafia assets.

text.p: Police said on Satuday they had seized $75 million of assets belonging to one of eastern Sicily's most feared Mafia clans.
The assets of Catania's Laudani family included bank deposits, flats and warehouses, six businesses, four villas and five fishing boats.

The judicial sequester was ordered by Catania magistrate Antonino Ferrara, who is leading an investigation into the clan which has been weakened by recent arrests after a bloody war with the Pillera family, their local rivals.

The Laudanis are also considerded close to the powerful Santapaola family, 79 of whose members were convicted on a variety of charges last Wednesday and sentenced to jail terms ranging from one to 22 years.
Clan leader Nitto Santapaola, who was not involved in the trial, is being tried in a separate case along with another 73 defendants charged with various crimes, including 22 murders.
